content.title: How to watch March Madness 2026: TV channels, live streams, full schedule
content.text: Updated: Mar. 19, 2026, 5:19 p.m.Published: Mar. 13, 2026, 11:15 a.m.A basketball with a March Madness logo rests on the rack prior to a second round of the NCAA college basketball tournament between Notre Dame and Michigan, Sunday, March 23, 2025, in South Bend, Ind. (AP Photo/John Mersits)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.The countdown to March Madness is on! Get ready to fill out those brackets and watch all the chaos and Cinderella stories unfurl that make this time of year so special. The best streaming option for all-in-one access to every channel needed to watch the NCAA tournament: DirecTV ChoiceThe best streaming option for access to every channel needed to watch just the men’s NCAA tournament: Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max bundleThe best streaming option for access to every channel needed to watch just the women’s NCAA tournament: Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundleThe 2026 NCAA men’s Tournament runs March 17 through April 6, while the NCAA women’s tournament runs March 18 through April 5. Below, we’ve compiled this handy guide to help you navigate everything you need to know to watch all the March Madness action. How to watch March Madness 2026 — At a glanceSelection SundayBrackets for both tournaments will be set on Selection Sunday, March 15. Here’s how to watch Selection Sunday for free:Watch the men’s Selection Sunday show for free with a DirecTV or FuboTV trial on CBS at 6 p.m. ET. Watch the women’s Selection Sunday show for free with a DirecTV or FuboTV trial on ESPN at 9 p.m. ET. Men’s and women’s NCAA March Madness tournamentAll 67 men’s tournament games will air across four networks: CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV. CBS games will also stream on Paramount+, while TBS, TNT and truTV games will also stream on HBO Max. For the women’s tournament, all 67 games will air across ESPN networks (ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU) and ABC. Every game can also be livestreamed on the ESPN App or on ESPN Unlimited. Here’s a breakdown of what channel each round of the women’s 2026 March Madness tournament will be streaming on:The First Four, first and second rounds are airing across ESPN networksSweet 16 and Elite Eight games are on ESPN and ABC.The Final Four game will air on ESPNThe championship game will air on ABCHow to watch March Madness 2026 for free (or almost free)Here’s a list of ways to watch tournament action for free:Pick up an OTA antenna: CBS and ABC broadcasts are available over the air with an indoor antenna, making it worth trying in most areas. Shop OTA antennas on AmazonWatch via the March Madness Live App: The official NCAA March Madness Live app offers one free hour of streaming per day before requiring a TV provider login. It’s enough to watch a half, and great for checking scores on mobile.Download the March Madness App from the App StoreDownload the March Madness App from the Google Play StoreUse free trials strategically: While they won’t last long enough to watch three weeks’ worth of tournament action, you can get a five-day free trial to DirecTV or FuboTV to watch some tournaments.Head to a sports bar: Your local sports bar is always a good option to watch games for free alongside other passionate basketball fans. How to watch March Madness 2026 on every deviceSmart TV / Streaming Stick Each streamer has an app available on all major smart TV platforms, including Roku, Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, Samsung Smart TVs and LG Smart TVs.iPhone & AndroidiPhone/iPad: Download your streaming app of choice from the App StoreAndroid: Download your streaming app of choice from Google PlayComputer / Browser Visit your streamer of choice’s direct website — no app download needed. Works on Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge.Casting to your TVMost apps support Chromecast (tap the Cast icon) and AirPlay (tap the AirPlay icon on iPhone/iPad). Start the stream on your phone and throw it to your living room TV in seconds.March Madness 2026 Full ScheduleCheck out the full schedule for both the men’s and women’s March Madness tournament. You can view brackets for the men’s NCAA tournament here and the women’s NCAA tournament here. (Live sports are not available with the Paramount+ Essential plan)For TBS/TNT/truTV and Final Four games: Sign up for a Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max bundle, starting at $19.99 per month. For women’s tournament: Sign up for the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundle for $35.99 per month. Want everything in one place?Sign up for DirecTV Choice for $59.99 (for the first month, then $94.99 every month following).
